title: POC scaling matrix workshop - Ledgerly pilot capacity planning
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on refining Dedicated sizing for the pilot. Reviewed last week's throughput results, exercised burst/fallback scenarios, adjusted autoscale thresholds, and agreed on a short benchmark to validate prefix KV cache benefits. Action items include sharing an updated sizing matrix, running a 1-hour stress test with 95th percentile target, and providing SOC2/KMS notes for secure ingest.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-22 15:30 UTC
- Duration: 48 min
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Ledgerly Head of Platform), Ethan Brooks (ML Eng), Samir Patel (CTO), Jenna Li (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick recap of throughput numbers, clear ask on burst runway and canary with KV prefix, small security checklist.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, I know this is the weekly pilot workshop. um quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya Rao: Priya here.
[00:09] Ethan Brooks: Ethan.
[00:10] Samir Patel: Samir.
[00:11] Jenna Li: Jenna.
[00:12] Diego Alvarez: Diego from Redwood.
[00:13] Maya Chen: Awesome. goal for today — review the test results from last sprint, agree on Dedicated sizing tweaks, and lock down a burst and fallback plan.

[00:30] Priya Rao: We had that 4 hour run last Thursday, right, we pushed a pretty spiky workload. numbers looked okay but the 95th latency jumped during the mid-run.
[00:40] Ethan Brooks: yeah the p95 went up to about 540 ms for generation tokens, avg was still about 220 ms. but throughput dropped when we hit the warm-up window, I think cache wasn't being used effectively.
[00:52] Diego Alvarez: okay that's consistent with what we saw — KV prefix cache wasn't enabled in that run, so each request was rebuilding some of the context. when we ran the small microtest with prefix caching we saw token throughput improve ~22% and p95 drop roughly 120 ms.
[01:10] Jenna Li: can you repeat that number, 22% is pretty material.
[01:12] Diego Alvarez: yep ~22% throughput increase in that micro-bench, p95 improved, but it was a short run so take with a grain.
[01:20] Samir Patel: so from an infra commitment standpoint, is it fair to say if we enable prefix KV we can reduce Dedicated nodes by one for the steady state?
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: possibly. depends on your QPS profile and how varied the prompts are. we modeled three matrices in the draft sizing sheet: conservative, typical, and cache-optimized. cache-optimized assumes heavy prompt similarity and KV reuse.
[01:45] Maya Chen: Diego, can you walk through the sizing matrix you prepared?
[01:48] Diego Alvarez: sure, pulling up a quick summary — (brief pause) — okay, conservative for your observed peak of 450 concurrent streams recommends 6 gpu instances with autoscale floor at 4, burst to 8 for traffic spikes. typical profile recommends 5 with floor 3 burst 7. cache-optimized recommends 4 with floor 2 burst 6. cost deltas per month are about 18% between conservative and typical, and another 14% savings to go cache-optimized.
[02:25] Priya Rao: that lines up with our cost targets. our finance guardrail wants monthly not exceed X, but we still need headroom for Black Friday style events — though our peak is not quite retail level.
[02:40] Ethan Brooks: one key callout — the run that showed high p95 coincided with a model switch at minute 52, we had a fallback from v1.3 to v1.1 and the warm start caused some KV eviction.
[02:55] Diego Alvarez: interesting, so a model variant rollback triggered cache thrash. good note. our routing can pin model variants to avoid that, or we can warm k-v for the fallback model in advance.
[03:10] Jenna Li: how do you warm KV at scale? that's operational overhead for our side.
[03:15] Diego Alvarez: we can do pre-warming using a short ramping job that hits common prompts, Redwood can supply a script, runs as a job in your staging cluster. takes ~10-15 minutes depending on size of the context.
[03:30] Maya Chen: also on fallback — we offer routing policies that, on capacity shortfall, send new sessions to a cheaper variant or to hosted fallback region to keep availability. that would meet your reliability goal without blowing Dedicated costs.
[03:46] Samir Patel: curious about the hosted fallback — data residency for those sessions? we can't have PII cross the region.
[03:52] Diego Alvarez: right, hosted fallback would be region-limited; for Ledgerly we'd pick a region in same jurisdiction and we'd disable persistent log capture for fallback sessions, we can also mask inputs. but we know this is sensitive so probably prefer model variant fallback within the Dedicated pool.
[04:10] Priya Rao: ok let's park hosted fallback, prefer variant fallback.
[04:14] Maya Chen: noted. Diego, we need a recommended autoscale policy with thresholds — what did you see as sweet spots?
[04:22] Diego Alvarez: from the runs, a target util of ~65% GPU utilization for scaling up works well to limit thrash. scale up on 2 consecutive 30s windows at >65%, and scale down after sustained <50% for 3 minutes. also add a short cooldown of 90s post-scale action.
[04:40] Ethan Brooks: that seems reasonable. is there a recommendation for burst provisioning vs autoscale? like a pre-warm burst runway?
[04:47] Diego Alvarez: yes — configure a burst reserve of 1-2 reserved nodes that can be spun up instantly and a scheduled ramp if you expect predictable spikes. for unpredictable spikes we'll rely on fast-launch nodes + routing to cheaper variants for new sessions.
[05:02] Jenna Li: what about cold start times, how fast are fast-launch nodes?
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: usually 45-75 seconds depending on model size and if the image is warmed. for LLM-medium it was ~60s in our tests.
[05:14] Priya Rao: ok so for a sudden surge we might see 60s of higher latency unless routing kicks in.
[05:18] Maya Chen: exactly which is why route-to-variant is recommended as an SLO-preserving measure.
[05:25] Samir Patel: any way to reduce that 60s? like keep a single minimal standby node?
[05:30] Diego Alvarez: yes that's the reserved small standby idea — cost vs recovery tradeoff. the sizing matrix includes a column for standby node cost.
[05:36] Priya Rao: one other risk — queueing behavior during scaling, we saw client timeouts at minute 12 of the last run. could be client-side retry logic that aggravated the tail.
[05:45] Ethan Brooks: we need to tune client retries and set an appropriate retry-backoff, also bump our client timeout to accommodate a short burst window.
[05:53] Maya Chen: note action there for ledgerly devs.
[05:55] (brief side chatter)
[06:05] Diego Alvarez: quick heads up on KV eviction — when we switch model binaries we may need to invalidate part of the cache. recommended practice is to namespace cache keys per model version so both can coexist during rollout. yeah it's a little extra memory but avoids warmup spikiness.
[06:25] Jenna Li: that sounds good, memory tradeoff ok.
[06:30] Priya Rao: let's build that into our rollout checklist.
[06:33] Maya Chen: security items — Priya had earlier questions around KMS and audit logs. Diego, can you summarize Redwood's current posture?
[06:42] Diego Alvarez: high level: we integrate with customer KMS providers via envelope encryption, keys never leave customer account for Private deployments; audit logs are shipped to your SIEM with configurable retention, and we support SSO/SAML, RBAC at token level. for Hosted there are additional caveats — SOC2 docs are in the security pack we'll share.
[07:05] Priya Rao: perfect, please send the SOC2 and KMS notes. we also require proof of key rotation policy for any customer-managed keys.
[07:12] Maya Chen: will send. action: Maya to attach security pack.
[07:16] Samir Patel: about cost — Diego you mentioned cost deltas. did you include cost of extra standby nodes and the pre-warm jobs?
[07:23] Diego Alvarez: yes the sizing matrix includes a small line for pre-warm job compute and standby node estimated delta; it's about 4-5% on top of baseline for the standby approach.
[07:34] Ethan Brooks: can we see the exact assumptions? request Diego to include the QPS distribution used in the model.
[07:40] Diego Alvarez: will do. I'll add a QPS histogram and the percentiles used for sizing.
[07:44] Priya Rao: great. next, the stress test plan — we want to simulate a 30-40% sudden ramp to test scale behavior and route policies.
[07:53] Maya Chen: proposal — run 1-hour test with three phases: ramp (10m), sustain spike (40m), cool-down (10m). measure p50/p95, error rate, and token cost delta. agreed?
[08:05] Jenna Li: yes, and include a phase where we toggle fallback to validate no PII crossing.
[08:11] Ethan Brooks: we'll also capture client retry behavior and include that in logs.
[08:15] Maya Chen: Diego will provision a canary with KV enabled for the test.
[08:19] Diego Alvarez: yes I'll stand up a canary in your staging namespace and enable namespace-keyed prefix cache and show comparative metrics.
[08:25] Priya Rao: timeline?
[08:27] Maya Chen: aim for the test to run by 2026-04-28. Redwood to share instrumentation checklist earlier.
[08:33] Samir Patel: anything on the legal/procurement front? we need a short addendum for burst SLAs and overage protection.
[08:40] Maya Chen: good call — I'll ask legal to draft a short pilot addendum with burst commitment and cost caps for the pilot.
[08:46] Priya Rao: and can we get a retention window for logs at least 90 days?
[08:50] Diego Alvarez: yes 90 days is fine for pilot, longer retention is an add-on.
[08:55] Maya Chen: ok wrapping — quick recap of decisions and owners.
[09:00] Maya Chen: decisions: 1) enable KV prefix cache for canary, 2) prefer variant fallback over hosted fallback, 3) adopt autoscale thresholds (scale up at >65% util windows), 4) run 1-hour stress test.
[09:14] Priya Rao: yep agreed.
[09:16] Ethan Brooks: agreed.
[09:18] Jenna Li: agreed.
[09:19] Diego Alvarez: I'll update the sizing matrix and share runbook links.
[09:23] Maya Chen: next steps — Diego will send updated sizing matrix by 2026-04-25, Maya will send security pack by 2026-04-24, Ledgerly to run test by 2026-04-28.
[09:35] Samir Patel: optional exec readout next week if the results are green.
[09:39] Priya Rao: knocking that up. thanks all.

(End of meeting, 48 minutes)

Notes: transcript may contain mis-hearings (Runway vs Runhouse), filler words. Referenced artifacts: sizing-matrix-v2.xlsx (to be shared), security-pack.pdf (SOC2/KMS notes), stress-test-runbook.md (instrumentation checklist).
